newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Tadiran net slides, but beats forecast.
newsitem.headline: Tadiran net slides, but beats forecast.

text.p: Tadiran Ltd, Israel's largest electronics company, Thursday reported sharply lower profits for the second quarter that were nonetheless above Wall Street's forecast.

It said it earned $14.1 million, or 72 cents a share, down from $53 million, or $2.70 a share, a year earlier, when it had a $33.7 million gain from the initial public offering of subsidiary Tadiran Telecommunications Ltd . Without the gain, the year-ago earnings per share would have been 98 cents.
Wall Street analysts had forecast 1997 second-quarter earnings per share of 62 cents.
The latest results include a capital gain of $2 million, mainly from the sale of a portion of its Tadiran Appliances Ltd subsidiary to Carrier Corp.
Sales in the quarter fell to $298.7 million from $311.4 million. But on a sequential basis, sales rose 8 percent from the first quarter of 1997 and by 11 percent from the last quarter of 1996.

All operating segments were profitable. Gross profits for the quarter, the highest recorded by the company, increased to 30.3 percent of sales from 27.2 percent last year, the company said, citing efficiency measures it implemented.

"Net income was negatively affected by an increase of $9 million net financing expenses this quarter, due primarily to the devaluation of the shekel and to hedging losses," Tadiran President and Chief Executive Israel Zamir said.

"Although we expect the devaluation to improve long-term profitability of export sales, it occurred too late in the quarter to materially affect second-quarter results. The devaluation significantly reduced the value of our shekel-based receivables."
Exports rose 23.8 percent to $173.9 million, representing 58 percent of total sales, against 45 percent last year.
Tadiran Telecom reported a 59 percent decline in sales to Bezeq Israel Telecom , which was largely offset by a 68 percent increase in export sales.
The company's backlog stands at $865 million, up $44.6 million since the end of 1996.
Tadiran is a subsidiary of Koor Industries Ltd, Israel's largest holding concern.
Tadiran's U.S. depositary receipts gained 50 cents to $32.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
